2010_006_051810regmtg.paragraph: Troy School District's Board of Education met in regular session on Tuesday, May 18, 2010 at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois. The packet is dominated by the April 2010 Treasurer's Report, which reports total disbursements in period of $21,820,077.17, including $18,053,329.16 in outgoing wire transfers, backed by the full check register and April year-to-date budget reports for every fund. The agenda also carries six purchasing awards charged mainly to the 2004 Capital Projects Fund, a resolution setting a June 15, 2010 public hearing on the proposed 2010-2011 budget, and a Section 624 resolution supporting the Oakland Intermediate School District budget.

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education, Regular Meeting, Tuesday, May 18, 2010, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000). Superintendent Barbara A. Fowler, Ph.D.; President Wendy Underwood; Secretary Nancy Philippart. The next meeting was announced for June 1, 2010 at Athens High School.

**Recognition and consent**
Item 2.A recognized employees retiring at the end of the 2009-2010 school year, among them Marcia Decker (Assistant Principal, Athens High School, 38 years), Rosalie Mallory (37), Marvin Thomas (Maintenance, 37) and Jane Drotos (35); Jasen Witt was to read each name and President Underwood present a clock and certificate. The consent agenda held the May 4 and May 11, 2010 minutes and the April Treasurer's Report. The May 4 minutes record Motion 10-038 (Outstanding Support Staff Award to Pam Byrd), 10-040 (two-year probationary contract to Janet Keeling as Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction, effective July 1, 2010) and 10-041 (flooring replacement to Conventional Carpet, $953,323.00, from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund), each carried 6-0 with Mrs. Philippart absent.

**Other**
A resolution set a public hearing on the proposed 2010-2011 budget for June 15, 2010 at 7:00 p.m., with notice at least six days ahead and the budget available for inspection June 7-11, 2010. Under Section 624 of the Revised School Code the board expressed support for the Oakland Intermediate School District budget solely for compliance purposes. Further resolutions authorized signing Michigan's Race to the Top memorandum of understanding before the May 21, 2010 MDE deadline and urged renewal of Oakland Community College's .8 mill levy at the August 3, 2010 primary. Anne Mull presented Fall 2009 MEAP results; a curriculum resolution proposed MME participation for all juniors, world language credit earned before high school effective with the class of 2014, and extra GPA weighting for AP courses effective with the class of 2011. Item 11.A proposed closed session under Public Act 267, Section 8(a) on the Superintendent's evaluation.

Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, Tuesday, May 18, 2010, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW). Superintendent Barbara A. Fowler, Ph.D.; President Wendy Underwood; Secretary Nancy Philippart; Michael M. Adamczyk, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services.

RECOGNITION (item 2.A). Retirees for the 2009-2010 school year included Marcia Decker (Assistant Principal, Athens High School, 38 years), Rosalie Mallory (Troy Union, 37), Marvin Thomas (Maintenance, 37), Keith Boman (36), Jane Drotos (Hamilton, 35), Gerald Carrier (34), Michael Heist (Boulan Park, 34), Leon Raczkowski (Costello, 34), Linda Ruks (Boulan Park, 34), Alan Walthall (33), Ruth Frushour (Athens, 32), Dale Bise (32), Gerald Pickle (32), Dave Sevcik (32), Jane Juett (Leonard, 30), Rosemary Morrow (Troy High, 28), Janis Hodgkins (Larson, 25), Kathleen Engelberts (23), Sharon Lennox (23), Jennifer Haglund (22), Monica Lamb (19), Eugenia Mikolajczak (17), Kathleen Danielson (Niles, 15) and Judy Mack (10). Monitors displayed a recognition for about twenty minutes beforehand; Jasen Witt read names and President Underwood presented a retirement clock and certificate.

CONSENT AND MINUTES. The May 4, 2010 meeting opened at 7:04 p.m. with Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti and Pochodylo present, Philippart absent, and about nine audience members. Motion 10-038 commended Pamela Byrd, a Teacher's Assistant from September of 1995 and Secretary since May of 1999 at Hamilton Elementary, as 2009-2010 Outstanding Support Staff Award recipient. Motion 10-039 approved the April 20, 2010 minutes and a fall athletic supplies bid. Motion 10-040 gave Janet Keeling a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure as Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction, effective July 1, 2010. Motion 10-041 awarded flooring replacement to Conventional Carpet at $953,323.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund. All votes were Yes 6, No 0, Philippart absent. Adamczyk presented the proposed Oakland Intermediate School District budget; Stuart Redpath and Anne Mull reported student survey results. Motion 10-042 entered closed session under Public Act 267, Section 8(c) at 8:24 p.m.; the board reconvened at 9:53 p.m. and adjourned at 9:55 p.m. Announcements covered the 34th Annual Student Art Show at Somerset North (May 3-16, 2010), a "The Sexting Society" town hall at Perspectives Counseling Center, 888 W. Big Beaver, on May 13, 2010, two Athens students with perfect ACT scores, thirteen schools honored as Green Schools, and nearly 5,000 students in grades 4 through 12 recognized at "Salute to Excellence." The May 11 workshop at the Administrative Center ran 6:00 p.m. to 11:40 p.m., covering food service, assistive technology, MEAP results, schools of choice and enrollment, and the preliminary 2010/2011 budget.

CURRICULUM. Item 7.A, "Fall 2009 MEAP Results - Trends in Results for Five Years of Grades 3-9 MEAP," was reported by Anne Mull, Director of Instruction and Assessment, covering grades 3 through 9 in math, reading, science and social studies with Troy, Oakland and Michigan trends for 05-06 through 09-10 and subgroup gap charts for students with IEPs (445), economically disadvantaged (679), Asian (1411), African American (247), Hispanic (66) and White (3322) students against an "All" group of 5277. Item 7.B proposed that all juniors participate in the Michigan Merit Exam toward graduation; that effective with the class of 2014 students passing full-year world language courses prior to high school receive credit toward the Michigan Merit Curriculum and district requirements; that effective with the class of 2011 Advanced Placement courses receive extra GPA weighting; and that adjusted grade point averages appear on transcripts beginning August 2010.

BUSINESS. Purchasing memos came from Frank E. Lams, Supervisor, Purchasing and Budget, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, 248-823-4052. Bid 9669, telephone system upgrades: 6 invited, 2 responding, opened April 21, 2010; Suntel Services at $53,254.81, split $51,208.66 to the 2004 Capital Projects Fund and $2,046.15 to the 2009/10 General Fund, the latter paid through a federally funded program covering the Career Center. Director of Technology Scott Bryan cited Mitel's end-of-life software; the bid as read was $51,600 and the corrected base bid $49,708.41, with mandatory alternates of $7,096.50 and ($7,125.00), a Career Center alternate of $1,485.90 approved by Dorothy Kaltz, voluntary alternates of $5,348.00 and $2,241.00, and a package discount of ($5,500.00), alternates subtotaling $3,546.40; line items included 19 Mitel 3340-to-3300 replacements at 2,395.50 each for 45,514.50 and a performance bond of 488.80. Bid 9670, lighting at Boulan Park and Larson Middle Schools and Athens High School: 3 invited, 4 responding, opened May 5, 2010, reviewed with Rae Killips of Integrated Design Solutions, 1441 West Long Lake, Suite 200, Troy; J.B. Electrical at $188,908.00 including the mandatory alternate. Bid 9671, paving at Barnard, Morse, Schroeder, Troy Union and Wass Elementary, Smith Middle School, Niles and the Services Building: 19 invited, 13 responding, opened April 29, 2010; Director of Maintenance Mondo Belardi rejected T & M Asphalt's $780,000.00 bid for using a different asphalt mix and recommended $759,474.00 split among Asphalt Specialists, Inc. $346,870.00 (Smith $134,420.00, Troy Union $106,290.00, Wass $106,160.00), Nagle Paving $278,990.00 (Niles Center $176,490.00, Barnard $102,500.00), Flynn Paving $99,199.00 (Schroeder) and Best Asphalt $34,415.00 (Admin Center/Services Building $24,900.00, Morse $9,515.00). Bid 9672, exterior door replacement: 14 invited, 3 responding, opened May 10, 2010; Peterson Glass Company of Ferndale was low at a combined $806,000.00, and Wold Architects (Chris Ziemer, LEED AP, 202 E. Third Street, Suite 200, Royal Oak, commission 104006) recommended rejecting the elementary and Smith packages and accepting Athens High School at $224,000 and Troy High School, tabulated at $34,300 but shown as $34,200 in the Wold letter's total of $258,200; the resolution awards $258,300.00. Bid 9648, Athens media center lounge furniture: 16 invited, 8 responding including two no bids, opened January 12, 2010, reviewed with Athens Principal Lara Dixon and Richard Machesky; SBD Commercial Interiors at $25,847.72 against Dew-El Corp. 34,616.70 and ASG 33,750.00. Bid 9674, acoustical wall panels at Boulan Park and Larson: 7 invited, 1 responding, opened May 11, 2010, reviewed with Director of Operations Ken Miller; PCI Industries at $33,200.00, $16,600.00 per building. Except for the telephone General Fund share, all awards are 2004 Capital Projects Fund expenditures. Item 8.G set a public hearing on the proposed 2010-2011 budget for 7:00 p.m., Tuesday, June 15, 2010 at the Services Building, with notice published at least six days beforehand carrying the 11-point bold statement that the property tax millage rate proposed to be levied will be a subject of the hearing, and copies available for inspection at 4400 Livernois, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., June 7 through June 11, 2010.

OTHER. Item 10.A: Section 624 of the Revised School Code requires the intermediate board to submit its proposed budget by May 1 and each constituent board to respond by June 1; Troy expressed support while stating that its support is for the sole purpose of complying with Section 624, with the resolution forwarded no later than June 1, 2010. Item 10.B authorized the board President and Superintendent to sign Michigan's Race to the Top memorandum of understanding, organized around standards and assessments, data systems to support instruction, great teachers and leaders, and turning around low performing schools, with a successful application estimated to bring $400 million dollars to the state, for submission to the MDE by the intermediate school district before the May 21, 2010 deadline. Item 10.C urged renewal of Oakland Community College's eight-tenths of one mill (.8 mill) ten-year levy at the August 3, 2010 primary, rolled back by the Headlee Amendment, noting OCC has educated more than 700,000 students since 1964. Item 10.D reported three incumbents filed for three Oakland Schools Board seats under Public Act 419 of 2004: Barbara DeMarco (six-year term), Connie Williams (six-year term) and Dr. Theresa Rich (partial two-year term); ballots are cast in person 6:30-7:15 p.m. Monday, June 7 in Conference Room A, 2111 Pontiac Lake Road, Waterford, absentee ballots prohibited, resolutions adopted no earlier than May 17, 2010 and faxed to 248.209.2206 by June 4, 2010 (contact Sherry McMillan, 248.209.2062). MCL 380.614 of Act 451 of 1976 is reproduced, with six-year terms beginning July 1, petition signature minimums of 6 to 20 below 10,000 population and 40 to 100 at 10,000 or more, and a nonrefundable $100.00 filing fee; the "Meet the Candidates" forum was cancelled because the incumbents were unopposed.

CLOSED SESSION. Item 11.A proposed a resolution under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(a) to discuss the Superintendent's evaluation, with a roll call of Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Pochodylo, Underwood and Edmunds and no further business other than adjournment. The next Board of Education meeting was set for June 1, 2010 at 7:00 p.m. at Athens High School.
